'''Melinda Jane Duer''' {{post-nominals|country=GBR|FRSC}} is Professor of Biological and Biomedical Chemistry in the [[Yusuf Hamied Department of Chemistry|Department of Chemistry]] at the [[University of Cambridge]], and was the first woman to be appointed to an academic position in the department. Her research investigates changes in molecular structure of the [[extracellular matrix]] in tissues in disease and during ageing. She served as Deputy Warden of [[Robinson College, Cambridge]] from 2016 to 2021.<ref>[https://www.robinson.cam.ac.uk/people/professor-melinda-j-duer College webpage]</ref> She is an editorial board member of the [[Journal of Magnetic Resonance]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Melinda Duer, PhD|url=https://www.journals.elsevier.com/journal-of-magnetic-resonance/editorial-board/melinda-duer-phd|access-date=2021-04-17|website=www.journals.elsevier.com}}</ref>

== Early life and education ==
Duer attended [[Sir James Smith's School]], a [[comprehensive school]] at Camelford, [[North Cornwall]].<ref name=":3">{{Cite web|title=Bone matters - researching the structure of bones|url=https://www.alumni.cam.ac.uk/news/bone-matters-researching-the-structure-of-bones|access-date=2021-04-17|website=Alumni|language=en}}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite interview|work=Chem@Cam|publisher=Yusuf Hamied Department of Chemistry, University of Cambridge|title=Q&A: Melinda Duer|last=Duer|first=Melinda|interviewer=Diane Harris|pages=22-23|issue=57|date=Spring 2018|url=https://www.ch.cam.ac.uk/chem-at-cam/57|access-date=7 October 2023|via=www.ch.cam.ac.uk}}</ref><ref name=":1">{{Cite web|date=2020-06-01|title=Professor Melinda Duer - Understanding the molecular structure of biological tissues|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bMHZBTd8HVY|access-date=2021-04-22|website=[[YouTube]]}}</ref> She enjoyed science there and was encouraged by her chemistry teacher to study [[Natural Sciences (Cambridge)|natural sciences]] at [[Emmanuel College, Cambridge]], where she specialized in chemistry.<ref name=":0" /> She was the first member of her family to attend higher education.<ref name=":1" /><ref>{{Cite web|title=Melinda Duer {{!}} Duer Research Group|url=https://www.ch.cam.ac.uk/group/duer/melinda-duer|access-date=2021-03-15|website=University of Cambridge}}</ref> Duer went on to complete her PhD in 1988 in [[theoretical chemistry]] with Malcolm Gerloch, in which she investigated [[ligand field theory]].<ref>{{Cite thesis|title=The Parametric Probes of Ligand Field Theory|date=1988|language=English|first=Melinda J.|last=Duer|oclc=53521744}}</ref>

== Research and career ==
During the course of her PhD research, Duer developed an interest in [[Nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy|nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy (NMR)]] while chatting with [[Lynn Gladden]] who frequently worked on the spectrometer in the room opposite Duer's office at the time. Towards the end of her PhD, Duer proposed using [[Solid-state nuclear magnetic resonance|solid-state NMR]] to investigate organometallic catalytic species in response to an advertised temporary lectureship in the department.<ref name=":2">{{Citation|last=Duer|first=Melinda J.|title=Duer, M. J.: The Power of Serendipity|date=2011-12-15|url=http://doi.wiley.com/10.1002/9780470034590.emrhp1086|encyclopedia=Encyclopedia of Magnetic Resonance|article-number=emrhp1086|editor-last=Harris|editor-first=Robin K.|place=Chichester, UK|publisher=John Wiley & Sons, Ltd|language=en|doi=10.1002/9780470034590.emrhp1086|isbn=978-0-470-03459-0|access-date=2021-04-22|url-access=subscription}}</ref> Thus, she became the first woman to be appointed to a lectureship in the [[Yusuf Hamied Department of Chemistry|Department of Chemistry]] at the [[University of Cambridge]] in 1988.<ref name=":0" /> In 1990, she was awarded a [[Royal Society University Research Fellowship]].<ref name=":2" /><ref>{{Cite web|title=Women in Chemistry, Melinda Duer {{!}} Yusuf Hamied Department of Chemistry|url=https://www.ch.cam.ac.uk/women-chemistry-melinda-duer|access-date=2021-03-15|website=University of Cambridge}}</ref>

In early 2000s, Duer pioneered the use of [[solid-state NMR]] to investigate biological tissues, including keratin<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Duer|first1=Melinda J.|last2=McDougal|first2=Nicky|last3=Murray|first3=Rachel C.|date=2003-06-19|title=A solid-state NMR study of the structure and molecular mobility of α-keratin|url=https://pubs.rsc.org/en/content/articlelanding/2003/cp/b302506c|journal=Physical Chemistry Chemical Physics|language=en|volume=5|issue=13|pages=2894–2899|doi=10.1039/B302506C|bibcode=2003PCCP....5.2894D |issn=1463-9084|url-access=subscription}}</ref> and bones,<ref>{{Cite web|title=Heavy mice and light things: using solid-state NMR spectroscopy to understand biological tissues in health and disease |website=University of Southampton|url=https://www.southampton.ac.uk/biosci/news/events/2020/01/29-heavy-mice-and-light-things.page|access-date=2021-03-15}}</ref> frequently obtained from horses due to her interest in [[Equestrianism|horse riding]].<ref name=":3" /> Her previous research on [[liquid crystal]] phases of polymers led her to wonder whether similar phases could form in [[keratin]].<ref name=":0" />

Duer has extensively investigated the [[extracellular matrix]], the component of biological tissues that simultaneously serves as the communication system between cells and provides a scaffold to support them. She is particularly interested in the molecular mechanisms that underpin the functions of the extracellular matrix. By understanding the structure-property relationships of biological tissue, Duer works to unravel the processes that give rise to collagenous tissue and [[Biomineralization|mineralisation]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Professor Melinda Duer {{!}} Yusuf Hamied Department of Chemistry|url=https://www.ch.cam.ac.uk/person/mjd13|access-date=2021-03-15|website=University of Cambridge|language=en}}</ref>

Duer has investigated the [[Calcification|calcification of blood vessels]] that occurs when people age.<ref name=":0" /> She proposed that the [[Atherosclerosis|hardening of arteries]] caused by the build-up of calcium may be triggered by polymeric [[adenosine diphosphate ribose]] (PAR), a molecule that is produced when the DNA inside cells is damaged.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2019-06-11|title=Mystery of why arteries harden may have been solved, say scientists|url=http://www.theguardian.com/science/2019/jun/11/mystery-arteries-harden-cracked-scientists-calcium-deposits|access-date=2021-03-15|website=The Guardian|language=en}}</ref> One of her graduate students launched a spin-out company, Cycle Pharmaceuticals, which provides personalised treatment to patients with [[Vascular disease|vascular diseases]].<ref name=":0" /> She was promoted to Professor in 2015.<ref name=":0" />

Duer was awarded the [[Royal Society of Chemistry]] [[Interdisciplinary Prizes (RSC)|Interdisciplinary Prize]] in 2017,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.rsc.org/news-events/articles/2017/may/awards-and-prizes-2017/|title=Prizes and awards 2017|access-date=2021-04-12|website=Royal Society of Chemistry |date=9 May 2017 }}</ref> and the [[Suffrage Science award]] in 2019.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2019-03-12|title=Suffrage Science Awards 2019: 12 role models in engineering & physical sciences awarded heirlooms|url=https://lms.mrc.ac.uk/suffrage-science-awards-2019-12-role-models-in-engineering-physical-sciences-awarded-heirlooms/|access-date=2021-04-17|website=LMS London Institute of Medical Sciences|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2019-07-08|title=A Suffrage Science Award for Professor Melinda Duer|url=https://www.robinson.cam.ac.uk/news/suffrage-science-award-professor-melinda-duer |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210417210920/https://www.robinson.cam.ac.uk/news/suffrage-science-award-professor-melinda-duer |archive-date=2021-04-17 |access-date=2021-04-17|website=Robinson College|language=en}}</ref>

=== Commercial ventures ===
Apart from licensing novel treatment for treating vascular disease to Cycle Pharmaceuticals,<ref>{{Cite web|last=|title=CYCLE Pharmaceuticals, The University of Cambridge and King's College London Partner to Repurpose PARP Inhibitor Drugs for Vascular Disease|url=https://cyclepharma.com/cycle-pharmaceuticals-the-university-of-cambridge-and-kings-college-london-partner-to-repurpose-parp-inhibitor-drugs-for-vascular-disease/|access-date=2021-04-14|website=Cycle Pharmaceuticals|date=19 December 2016 |language=en-GB}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Cambridge Enterprise licenses PARP inhibitor drug IP to Cycle Pharmaceuticals|url=https://www.enterprise.cam.ac.uk/news/cambridge-enterprise-licenses-parp-inhibitor-drug-ip-cycle-pharmaceuticals/|access-date=2021-04-14|website=Cambridge Enterprise|language=en-GB}}</ref> Duer is a co-founder of Cambridge Oncology Ltd.<ref>{{Cite web|title=CAMBRIDGE ONCOLOGY LTD - Officers (free information from Companies House)|url=https://find-and-update.company-information.service.gov.uk/company/11658105/officers|access-date=2021-04-14|website=find-and-update.company-information.service.gov.uk|language=en}}</ref>

=== Mentoring and international development ===

Duer is part of the Strategic Advisory Group of the Cambridge-Africa Programme, an initiative by the University of Cambridge to strengthen research capacity with African universities and research institutions.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Cambridge-Africa Governance :: Cambridge-Africa|url=https://www.cambridge-africa.cam.ac.uk/about/cambridge-africa-governance/|access-date=2021-04-15|website=www.cambridge-africa.cam.ac.uk}}</ref> In this role, Duer mentors African academics such as Dr Mercy Badu of [[Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Africa Research Excellence Fund (AREF) on LinkedIn: LMS launches scheme to mentor African female scientists|url=https://www.linkedin.com/posts/africaresearchexcellencefund_lms-launches-scheme-to-mentor-african-female-activity-6775027371734028288-BQZF|access-date=2021-04-15|website=www.linkedin.com|language=en}}</ref>

As a previous holder of the Suffrage Science award, Duer nominated Dr Mary Anti Chama of the [[University of Ghana]] for the same award in 2021.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2021-03-08|title=Leading women in 'Engineering and Physical Sciences' win Suffrage Science award on the scheme's tenth anniversary|url=https://lms.mrc.ac.uk/leading-women-in-engineering-and-physical-sciences-win-suffrage-science-award-on-the-schemes-tenth-anniversary/|access-date=2021-04-17|website=LMS London Institute of Medical Sciences|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|date=2021-03-12|title=Dr. Mary Anti Chama Receives Suffrage Science Award|url=https://www.ug.edu.gh/news/dr-mary-anti-chama-receives-suffrage-science-award|access-date=2021-04-17}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|date=2021-03-10|title=Suffrage Science Awards 2021: A Celebration of Women Changing Science|url=https://lms.mrc.ac.uk/suffrage-science-awards-2021-a-celebration-of-women-changing-science/|access-date=2021-04-17|website=LMS London Institute of Medical Sciences|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Twitter status Mar 8, 2021. MRC London Institute of Medical Sciences|url=https://twitter.com/mrc_lms/status/1368920130848178177|access-date=2021-04-17|website=Twitter|language=en}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
Duer used to be an [[Equestrianism|equestrian]], and has said that her interest in biological chemistry started with studying keratin in [[Horse hoof|horses hooves]] and understanding leg fractures in one of her rescue horses.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" />  Her other interests include [[Cycling|cycling]] and competing in [[Triathlon|triathlons]].
